SE to run 48-hour Dedicated benchmark and share results by 2026-07-28
Customer to confirm internal pricing approval path by 2026-07-29

summary: Procurement-focused call to review Redwood MSA/DPA, discuss SLAs and pricing approval path. Customer has security and data residency constraints; requested redlines and a Dedicated pilot benchmark. Agreed next steps: Redwood to send redlined contracts and SOC2, SE to run performance test, customer to circulate pricing to finance.
transcript:
Header: Date: 2026-07-22 | Start: 14:00 PT | Duration: 1:02:15 | Meeting ID: ff-20260722-8792
Attendees: Claire Hsu (Redwood AE), Rajat Mehta (Redwood SE), Maria Alvarez (Seabright - Head of Security), Tom Reed (Seabright - Procurement), Jamal Carter (Seabright - CTO)

[00:00] Claire (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for making time. Quick roll call - we're recording this so we can capture the redlines and action items.
[00:12] Maria: Yep, thanks. We have Tom and Jamal here as well, we'll be focused mostly on the contract and security items.
[00:20] Claire: Great. Agenda - go through the MSA and DPA redlines you've sent, cover SLA expectations and credits, clarify pricing approval path and pilot scope, and list required vendor docs. Sound right?
[00:30] Tom: Correct. We also want to confirm onboarding timeline assuming we sign.

[01:05] Rajat (Redwood SE): I'll jump in on the technical parts where needed - especially for Dedicated and on-prem options.

[02:15] Maria: We sent the redlines to the DPA that require data residency - Seabright requires PHI to remain in us-east-1, and KMS-backed encryption with customer-managed keys if possible. Does Redwood support HSM/KMS integrations?
[02:35] Rajat: Yes, we support both cloud KMS and customer-managed keys for Private deployments; for Redwood Dedicated we can configure KMS via customer KMS or bring-your-own-HSM in the VPC option. The hosted API can use Redwood-managed keys but we do offer enterprise KMS integrations on the Private offering.
[02:55] Maria: Ok the DPA redline asks for that explicitly. Also we asked for 7 years audit log retention for certain endpoints - is that feasible?
[03:10] Rajat: Audit log retention is configurable; long retention increases storage cost but technically fine. For hosted customers we typically do 1 year by default; we can extend to 7 years on Dedicated/Private with an add-on. We'll put cost notes in the pricing note.

[04:00] Tom: On the MSA, we have a standard limitation of liability clause cap that is higher than Redwood's standard. We're asking for 5M for critical vendors. Is Redwood flexible?
[04:15] Claire: We can entertain a negotiated liability cap tied to committed spend and term; typically higher caps map to enterprise agreements with an ARR commitment. What level of spend are you forecasting?
[04:30] Tom: For year one, if pilot converts, ~$600k annualized. We can consider a 12- or 24-month committed Dedicated contract.
[04:45] Claire: Good, that gives us levers. I'll flag this to legal and propose a tiered cap: standard, and an elevated cap when you commit to reserved capacity. We'll include that in the redline package.

[06:10] Maria: Regarding SLA, we need 99.9% uptime for inference endpoints plus token latency P95 under 300ms for standard routes. If you can't guarantee that on hosted, we'll need fallback to Dedicated or Private.
[06:30] Rajat: 99.9% is reasonable for Dedicated with reserved pools; hosted offers best-effort with SLOs but not SLA-backed for low tiers. For the P95 latency 300ms - that depends on model size, sequence length, and concurrency. For small-medium models on Dedicated we can meet that, but we should run a benchmark.
[06:50] Jamal (CTO): Can you run a benchmark that mimics our workload? We have average sequence length ~1k tokens for summarization and 3k tokens for long-form generation, concurrency spikes to 200 rps for a short window.
[07:05] Rajat: Yes, we can. We'll need to know model families (open or closed) and whether you need KV caching/continuous batching enabled. We'll propose a 48-hour load test using a model that approximates your production model and share throughput/latency numbers.
[07:25] Jamal: We'll send a sample prompt set and token distribution.

[08:00] Tom: Pricing approval - our finance requires a formal quote and a breakdown of committed vs usage pricing, and an approval path that includes security healthy check. Who signs final quote?
[08:15] Claire: We'll send a formal quote with a dedicated pricing line for reserved capacity and an overage plan. For the MSA we can include an appendix with pricing and SKUs. Final signature typically by your procurement/finance - we can route countersignature via DocuSign.
[08:35] Tom: We want a 60-day review period post-sign to run the pilot and validate perf before 12-month commit - is that acceptable?
[08:50] Claire: We can do a pilot with a letter of intent; pilot terms can include a pause in billing for certain pilot credits. If pilot converts, credits apply to committed spend. We'll capture exact terms in the redline.

[09:40] Maria: A few security checklist items - SOC2 Type II report, ISO27001, penetration test summary, incident response contacts, and SSO/SAML support with SCIM for provisioning.
[09:55] Rajat: We have SOC2 Type II and ISO attestation; pen test summaries can be shared under an NDA. We support SAML 2.0 SSO and SCIM for user provisioning on the Console. Audit logs and per-request tracing are available.
[10:20] Maria: For data residency, we also need assurance that backups will not be replicated outside region and that log exports are region-limited.
[10:35] Rajat: On Dedicated/Private we can keep backups and logs in the customer's VPC/region. On hosted, we'd need to scope it out - we do have region controls for EU/US but not per-customer isolated backup storage unless it's a Private offering.

[12:00] Tom: Any concerns about regulatory compliance? We operate in healthcare and need HIPAA support.
[12:10] Claire: We are comfortable executing a BAA for PHI for Dedicated/Private deployments. For hosted, we evaluate per-customer - but Dedicated gives clearer controls. We'll add BAA language and the DPA redlines.

[15:00] Maria: Penalty clauses - in the SLA we want service credits for downtime above the SLA. Typical ask is pro-rata credits against monthly fees.
[15:15] Claire: That's standard. Our SLA includes credits tied to monthly uptime percentage bands. We'll propose specific credit bands in the MSA appendix. For higher credits tied to elevated liability caps we'll need to reflect that in negotiated terms.

[17:20] Jamal: On onboarding, we need a checklist: network requirements (VPC peering or IP ranges), certs, SCIM details, and runbook for failover.
[17:35] Rajat: We'll share an onboarding checklist and a runbook. For Dedicated we do initial config, network egress IPs, and can support transit and private connectivity.

[19:00] Tom: Procurement noise - finance will want to see price waterfall and cost of long-term commit vs overage. Also payment terms - 30 vs 45 days?
[19:15] Claire: Standard is 30 net; for enterprise we can discuss 45/60 with a credit check or prepay. We'll note that in the quote.

[21:00] Maria: Can you confirm retention of logs and ability to provide audit exports within 48 hours on request?
[21:10] Rajat: Yes, audit exports can be provided; on Dedicated we'll enable API access for exports and can ship bulk logs to your S3 in-region. We'll document the process.

[25:00] (minor crosstalk) Speaker 1 (transcription artifact): um sorry to interrupt, Claire you mentioned pilot credits?
[25:10] Claire: Yes, pilot credits - we typically offer credits that offset a portion of usage for a 30-90 day pilot depending on scope. For a Dedicated pilot we'd likely offer a combination of credits plus discounted commitment if you sign within the pilot window.

[28:50] Tom: Contract redlines - we have a standard clause for right to audit. We want to preserve that in the DPA. How do you accommodate external audits?
[29:05] Claire: We allow audit rights with reasonable notice and scope; for hosted customers we provide attestation and SOC2 artifacts. For Dedicated/Private we can do on-site or remote audit for specific controls under NDA. We'll put proposed language in the redline.

[34:40] Maria: A question on model variants/fallbacks - if we run in hosted and a region outage occurs, can we route to a different region with same data protections?
[34:55] Rajat: Routing to a different region is possible but it may conflict with residency requirements for PHI. For PHI workloads we'd recommend Dedicated in the required region or Private. We can implement policy-based routing with fallback only to compliant regions.

[40:00] Jamal: For the performance test scope - can Redwood show perf for quantized models vs float models and give per-token cost estimates?
[40:15] Rajat: Yes, we'll include benchmarks for quantized and fp16 variants, show throughput/latency and cost per 1k tokens under different batching profiles.

[45:20] Tom: Any outstanding legal exceptions from Redwood's side?
[45:30] Claire: Nothing unusual beyond standard indemnification and IP language. We'll actually propose some tailored indemnity language for regulated workloads. Legal will produce the redline bundle.

[49:10] Maria: We need an escrow mechanism for critical models/code if this becomes core infra - do you offer vendor escrow?
[49:25] Claire: We don't by default but we can discuss vendor escrow options for Licensed bits in Private deployments. I'll flag to legal and partnerships.

[53:00] (brief silence as docs are referenced)
[53:10] Rajat: I'll also include a playbook for failover and KV cache behavior during outages - we find customers are particularly sensitive to token cost spikes during retries.
[53:25] Jamal: Good, include guidance on batching and cache TTL.

[58:00] Claire: Quick recap before we close - action items: Redwood will send redlined MSA and DPA and SOC2/ISO attestations by Friday 2026-07-24; SE (Rajat) will run a 48-hour Dedicated benchmark and share results by 2026-07-28; Seabright will confirm internal approvers and provide sample prompt set by 2026-07-24; procurement will confirm desired payment terms and pilot acceptance criteria by 2026-07-29.
[58:30] Tom: Sounds right. We'll aim to review the redlines within 48 hours of receipt.
[59:00] Maria: One more - please include a clear appendix on data residency and backup storage locations in the DPA redline.
[59:15] Claire: Noted, we'll add that.
[61:00] Claire: Thanks everyone - we'll follow up with the package and schedule the pilot kickoff once the benchmark is scheduled.
[61:10] Tom: Thanks all.

End of recording.
